title: 1973 AHSME Problem 16
statement: If the sum of all the angles except one of a convex polygon is \(2190^\circ,\) then the number of sides of the polygon must be

solutions.text:
If the omitted angle is \(x^\circ,\) then convexity gives \(0\lt x\lt180.\) Hence \[ 180(n-2)=2190+x, \] so \[ \frac{2190}{180} \lt n-2 \lt\frac{2370}{180}. \] This is \[ 12\frac16\lt n-2\lt13\frac16. \] The only possible integer is \(n-2=13,\) so \(n=15.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Let the omitted interior angle be \(x^\circ\) and the number of sides be \(n\)
Use \(0\lt x\lt180\) to trap the integer \(n-2\) in an interval of length \(1\)
